title: Health & at the Doctor's
cefrDescriptors: Can describe symptoms and say where it hurts (avoir mal à).
Can understand and follow a doctor's simple advice and instructions.
concept:
The doctor's visit is a classic DELF A2 scene, and it runs on one small machine: avoir mal à — literally 'to have pain at'. The à contracts with the article exactly the way you learned in A1:
  à + le → au : J'ai mal au ventre. (My stomach hurts.)
  à + la → à la : J'ai mal à la tête. (I have a headache.)
  à + les → aux : J'ai mal aux dents. (My teeth hurt.)
So the pattern is J'ai mal + au/à la/à l'/aux + body part. No possessive — French says 'THE head', not 'my head'.

How long has it hurt? French uses depuis + the PRESENT tense where English uses 'have been':
  J'ai mal à la gorge depuis deux jours. (My throat has hurt for two days.)
  Je tousse depuis lundi. (I've been coughing since Monday.)

How do you feel overall? The reflexive se sentir: Je me sens fatigué(e). Je ne me sens pas bien.

At the surgery, the doctor examines you (examiner), takes your temperature — la fièvre is fever — and ends with advice you already know how to build from A2.1:
  Il faut vous reposer. / Vous devez boire de l'eau.
  Je vous prescris un médicament. (I'm prescribing you a medicine.)
The paper the doctor hands you is une ordonnance (a prescription — a famous false friend: it is NOT an 'ordinance'), and you take it to la pharmacie.

The cast of the scene: le médecin (doctor), un rendez-vous (appointment), un symptôme, la grippe (flu), un rhume (a cold), tousser (to cough), la gorge (throat), le dos (back), le ventre (stomach), la tête (head).

Role-play both sides out loud: the patient states two symptoms with j'ai mal and depuis; the doctor answers with one il faut and one je vous prescris.
